page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-2xL4 is an x86_64 architecture server virtualized via the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 vCPUs with a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per vCPU.

This server integrates hardware acceleration via two NVIDIA L4 GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture family. Together, these GPUs provide a total of 48 GB of VRAM. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, meaning storage resources must be attached externally. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The primary tradeoff of this configuration is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce performance variability under sustained CPU-bound workloads compared to dedicated core instances. However, the high memory capacity combined with dual NVIDIA L4 GPUs makes this server suitable for memory-intensive GPU workloads, such as machine learning inference, data science jobs, and graphics rendering, where GPU and RAM capacity are prioritized over dedicated host CPU performance.
